findings.source_passage: What would be a great blessing is to wake up from this horrible nightmare. Even knowing I had to go back to work would be better than this junk about lords and ladies, and curses and blessings with no benefit and plenty of punishment.
findings.source_locator: After 'What kind of a favor is that?' exchange, before 'His face softened'
findings.why_it_matters: This extended tirade is the heroine's signature voice in full flight—colloquial, self-deprecating, grounding the fantasy in mundane reality ('go back to work'). Its absence strips the scene of a key register-defining moment that distinguishes this narrator's comic, contemporary voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full rant verbatim or very closely: 'What would be a great blessing is to wake up from this horrible nightmare. Even knowing I had to go back to work would be better than this junk about lords and ladies, and curses and blessings with no benefit and plenty of punishment.'

findings.source_passage: His manner was quiet and calm, as though he spoke to a wild creature. I must admit I was ready to bolt out the window, even if the drop was a good sixty feet.
findings.source_locator: Paragraph beginning 'His manner was quiet and calm'
findings.why_it_matters: The narratorial aside ('I must admit I was ready to bolt out the window, even if the drop was a good sixty feet') is a signature self-aware interjection that establishes the narrator's ironic, confessional tone and keeps the comedy alive during an otherwise tense exchange. Its loss flattens the heroine's perspective.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert the parenthetical narrative aside, either verbatim or equivalently, when the lord speaks 'quietly and calmly as though to a wild creature.'

findings.source_passage: I snorted. That was getting to be a habit.
findings.source_locator: After 'The Lady's favor is a great blessing and is rarely given.'
findings.why_it_matters: The self-aware aside ('That was getting to be a habit') is a small but characteristic marker of the narrator's self-deprecating comic voice; its repeated absence across this exchange contributes to cumulative voice erosion.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the brief narratorial commentary when the heroine snorts in response to the dragon lord's insistence on the Lady's favor.

summary: The draft is broadly faithful, preserving most signature lines and plot beats, but loses two voice-establishing digressions mid-scene—the heroine's 'go back to work' tirade and the 'wild creature / sixty-foot drop' aside—that are medium-severity flattening of the narrator's signature comic register.
